question_text: Explain how dependency injection works in FastAPI and why it is useful.
answer_text: FastAPI uses Depends() to declare dependencies on path operations or other dependencies. FastAPI resolves the dependency graph per request, caches results within the same request by default, supports yield-based dependencies for setup/teardown like DB sessions, and makes testing easy via app.dependency_overrides.
retrieved_context: FastAPI dependency injection uses Depends() to share logic, database connections, and auth checks, with support for yield cleanup and dependency_overrides in tests.

question_text: Why is accuracy alone misleading on imbalanced classification datasets?
answer_text: Accuracy is only bad because neural networks cannot compute percentages on binary labels.
retrieved_context: On imbalanced datasets, predicting the majority class yields high accuracy while failing on the minority class; precision, recall, F1, and PR-AUC are more informative.

question_text: How can you detect overfitting during model training?
answer_text: You can spot it when the model keeps getting better on the training split while its error on a held-out validation set levels off or starts getting worse.
retrieved_context: Overfitting occurs when training loss decreases while validation loss increases.

question_text: Compare stateful server sessions and stateless JWTs for API authentication, including revocation trade-offs.
answer_text: Sessions store state on the server and JWTs store claims in a signed token sent by the client.
retrieved_context: JWTs avoid server-side session lookups but are harder to revoke before expiration without a denylist or short TTL + refresh token rotation.
